summary: This bill renames the VA community-based outpatient clinic in Lubbock, Texas, as the General Bernie Mittemeyer VA Clinic and requires all U.S. government references to use the new name.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a purely ceremonial measure to rename an existing VA clinic. It does not authorize, appropriate, or alter any government funds or spending levels.
No provisions in the bill relate to tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue collection of any kind.
While the bill references a VA healthcare facility, it only changes the facility's name and makes no changes to coverage, delivery models, funding mechanisms, or public vs. private healthcare policy.
The legislation contains no language concerning firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No content addresses immigration policy, border security, visas, or related protections.
The bill does not mention or affect reproductive health services or abortion access.
The bill names a VA outpatient clinic after a retired general but does not alter military budgets, force structure, or defense policy.
No environmental regulations, protections, or energy provisions are present.
Although VA clinics serve veterans, the bill is limited to a name change and does not expand, contract, or modify any benefits programs.
The legislation has no connection to schools, education funding, or school choice policies.
No references to controlled substances, enforcement, or decriminalization appear in the text.
The bill does not address sentencing, policing, incarceration, or justice reform.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization measures are involved.
The measure has no fiscal impact and does not address deficits or debt reduction.
No provisions relate to legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
The bill contains nothing concerning foreign assistance or international aid.
No election procedures, voting access, or integrity measures are addressed.
The legislation does not touch on technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No labor, union, or workplace policy provisions are included.
The bill makes no reference to religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination rules.
